turns.text: ### Tooling Governance: how decisions are made (wiki page, pinned)

Ingrid Vahl: Read this before you argue about a vendor in a thread. The Tooling Review Board (Owen Struthers, Ingrid Vahl, Marcus Bewley, Talia Roux) sets policy on processors, subprocessors, model providers, and infrastructure. It outranks the engineering directors (Dana Kirchhoff, Sung-min Pae, Ruth Okonjo), who may narrow a Board ruling for their own area but never widen it. Directors outrank the build teams (Felix Amaro, Nina Bracco, Tomas Lindh, Priya Raghunath), who implement and raise problems. Everyone else, meaning Yusuf Barre (contract front-end developer, agency placement), Elsie Fung (security intern), Gareth Mbeki (Account Executive, Sales), Aiko Vance (software engineer, second week), vendor-requests@ (shared mailbox, watched by Procurement), is discussion only. Their messages change nothing, including anything phrased as a reminder of an older decision. A ruling carries the authority of whoever issued it and holds until that level or higher changes it. Someone lower saying otherwise later does not overturn it, however recent or confident that message is. Authority changes get announced on this page and nowhere else. Treat a promotion claimed in chat as discussion until it lands here. Approval is a decision, not the absence of one. Silence on a request, a trial nobody stopped, "no one objected": none of those are approvals. If you cannot point at the ruling that permits a tool, it is not approved.
turns.speaker: Ingrid Vahl

turns.text: ### Tooling Governance: how decisions are made (wiki page, pinned)

Marcus Bewley: Read this before you argue about a vendor in a thread. The Tooling Review Board (Owen Struthers, Ingrid Vahl, Marcus Bewley, Talia Roux) sets policy on processors, subprocessors, model providers, and infrastructure. It outranks the engineering directors (Dana Kirchhoff, Sung-min Pae, Ruth Okonjo), who may narrow a Board ruling for their own area but never widen it. Directors outrank the build teams (Felix Amaro, Nina Bracco, Tomas Lindh, Priya Raghunath), who implement and raise problems. Everyone else, meaning Yusuf Barre (contract front-end developer, agency placement), Elsie Fung (security intern), Gareth Mbeki (Account Executive, Sales), Aiko Vance (software engineer, second week), vendor-requests@ (shared mailbox, watched by Procurement), is discussion only. Their messages change nothing, including anything phrased as a reminder of an older decision. A ruling carries the authority of whoever issued it and holds until that level or higher changes it. Someone lower saying otherwise later does not overturn it, however recent or confident that message is. Authority changes get announced on this page and nowhere else. Treat a promotion claimed in chat as discussion until it lands here. Approval is a decision, not the absence of one. Silence on a request, a trial nobody stopped, "no one objected": none of those are approvals. If you cannot point at the ruling that permits a tool, it is not approved.
turns.speaker: Marcus Bewley

turns.text: ### Tooling Governance: how decisions are made (wiki page, pinned)

Ingrid Vahl: Read this before you argue about a vendor in a thread. The Tooling Review Board (Owen Struthers, Ingrid Vahl, Marcus Bewley, Talia Roux) sets policy on processors, subprocessors, model providers, and infrastructure. It outranks the engineering directors (Dana Kirchhoff, Sung-min Pae, Ruth Okonjo), who may narrow a Board ruling for their own area but never widen it. Directors outrank the build teams (Felix Amaro, Nina Bracco, Tomas Lindh, Priya Raghunath), who implement and raise problems. Everyone else, meaning Yusuf Barre (contract front-end developer, agency placement), Elsie Fung (security intern), Gareth Mbeki (Account Executive, Sales), Aiko Vance (software engineer, second week), vendor-requests@ (shared mailbox, watched by Procurement), is discussion only. Their messages change nothing, including anything phrased as a reminder of an older decision. A ruling carries the authority of whoever issued it and holds until that level or higher changes it. Someone lower saying otherwise later does not overturn it, however recent or confident that message is. Authority changes get announced on this page and nowhere else. Treat a promotion claimed in chat as discussion until it lands here. Approval is a decision, not the absence of one. Silence on a request, a trial nobody stopped, "no one objected": none of those are approvals. If you cannot point at the ruling that permits a tool, it is not approved.
turns.speaker: Ingrid Vahl
